items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But the big bands you’re talking about, like Ellington and Lunceford and Benny Goodman – there were a lot of ballrooms at that time.

ctx.x: This is the trio. This is Stuff Smith’s trio, the group that I came to New York with.
In terms of this era and that time, you had Duke Ellington coming in to Chicago, and Jimmie Lunceford, and who?

Yes, they came, but that was – they came into Chicago to play ballrooms, like the Savoy Ballroom, and play theaters, like the Regal Theater, in that period of time that you’re speaking of, when their bands came in. But the local groups worked at these clubs for long periods of time. They stayed in one club for a very long period. But the big bands you’re talking about, like Ellington and Lunceford and Benny Goodman – there were a lot of ballrooms at that time. Ballroom dancing was a thing. So you had bands that…
